title: ‘प्रेमदासको डायरी’ उपन्यासमा आलोचनात्मक यथार्थवाद [Critical Realism in the Novel 'Premdas's Diary']
nepali: यो लेखमा आलोचनात्मक यथार्थवादी कोणबाट उपन्यासकार रेशम विरहीको ‘‘प्रेमदासको डायरी’ उपन्यासको विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । यहाँ उपन्यासको विश्लेषणका लागि सैद्धान्तिक ढाँचा तयार पारिएको छ । यसका लागि आलोचनात्मक यथार्थवादको पुष्टि गर्ने कुञ्जी पनि तयार पारिएको छ । यसमा उपन्यासको कथावस्तुको सन्दर्भ उठाउँदै साक्ष्य सङ्कलन गरिएको छ । नेपालमा चलेका पञ्चायती व्यवस्था, २०३६ सालको आन्दोलन, २०३७ सालको जनमतसङ्ग्रह, २०४६ सालको जनआन्दोलन, २०५२ देखि २०६२ सम्म भएको माओवादी क्रान्ति र त्यसपछिको गणतन्त्र प्राप्तिले गरिब जनताको पक्षमा खासै परिवर्तन नल्याएको कुरा यो उपन्यासमा गरिएको छ । यो उपन्यासमा आएका तिनै घटनालाई हेर्दै सामन्तवादी सामाजिक व्यवस्थाप्रति आलोचना गर्ने, राजनैतिक व्यवस्थाप्रति आलोचना गर्ने, वर्गव्यवस्थाप्रति आलोचना गर्ने, विभेदयुक्त जातीय व्यवस्थाप्रति आलोचना गर्ने, मानवता विरोधी कार्यप्रति आलोचना गर्ने र नारीमाथि गरिने शोषणप्रति आलोचना गर्ने काम यो लेखभित्र गरिएको छ ।
american_english: In this article, the novel 'Premdas's Diary' by novelist Resham Birahi has been analyzed from the angle of critical realism. Here, a theoretical framework has been prepared for analyzing the novel. For this, a key to confirming critical realism has also been prepared. In this, evidence has been collected by raising the context of the novel's subject matter. The fact that the Panchayat system prevalent in Nepal, the 2036 movement, the 2037 referendum, the 2046 people's movement, the Maoist revolution from 2052 to 2062, and the republic attained thereafter brought no real change in favor of the poor people has been presented in this novel. Looking at those very events in this novel, this article critiques the feudal social order, the political system, the class system, the discriminatory caste system, inhumane actions, and the exploitation of women.
british_english: This article analyses the novel 'Premdas's Diary' by the novelist Resham Birahi from the standpoint of critical realism. A theoretical framework has been prepared here for the analysis of the novel. To this end, a key establishing critical realism has also been prepared. Evidence has been gathered here by raising the context of the novel's subject matter. The fact that the Panchayat system prevailing in Nepal, the 2036 uprising, the 2037 referendum, the 2046 People's Movement, the Maoist revolution of 2052 to 2062, and the republic attained thereafter brought no significant change in favour of the poor people is presented in this novel. Looking at those very events in this novel, this article undertakes critiques of the feudal social order, of the political system, of the class system, of the discriminatory caste system, of inhuman actions, and of the exploitation of women.
australian_english: This article analyses novelist Resham Birahi's novel 'Premdas's Diary' from a critical realist standpoint. A theoretical framework has been drawn up here for analysing the novel. A key for confirming critical realism has been drawn up as well. Evidence has been collected by raising the context of the novel's storyline. This novel presents the fact that the Panchayat system that ran in Nepal, the 2036 movement, the 2037 referendum, the 2046 Jana Andolan, the Maoist revolution from 2052 to 2062, and the republic that came afterwards brought no appreciable change in favour of the poor people. Taking in those very events in the novel, this article proceeds to critique the feudal social order, the political system, the class system, the discriminatory caste system, anti-human activity, and the exploitation of women.
informal_english: So this article digs into novelist Resham Birahi's novel 'Premdas's Diary' from a critical realist angle. Here, a theoretical framework gets set up to analyse the novel. And to help with that, a key to nailing down critical realism has been put together too. Evidence has been gathered by bringing up the context of the novel's storyline. The novel puts forward that the Panchayat system in Nepal, the 2036 movement, the 2037 referendum, the 2046 people's movement, the Maoist revolution from 2052 to 2062, and the republic that came after it all did pretty much nothing for the poor. Taking a look at those very events, this article goes ahead and critiques the feudal social order, the political system, the class system, the discriminatory caste system, inhumane actions, and the exploitation of women.
translator_notes: Doubled opening quote in source ('‘‘प्रेमदासको डायरी') treated as a single quote. All years (2036, 2037, 2046, 2052, 2062) are Bikram Samvat years and are reproduced as numerals; 2046 Jan Andolan = 1990 people's movement, 2052–2062 = 1996–2006 Maoist conflict. 'रेशम विरही' transliterated as 'Resham Birahi'; novel title kept as 'Premdas's Diary' per batch gloss. Strict 6-sentence order preserved. Informal flavour: Canadian casual.
